title: Wooden Joe's power and playing advertising jobs
summary: Joe could outblow the street alone; Robinson did advertising jobs with him and made records once.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: You say Wooden Joe was so powerful, did you play with him on the street too sometime?

I'm telling you, sometimes on the street, we used to wonder. He hired a couple of corner players and if they ain't there any time to leave, he'd leave out there by himself. That was one powerful man. I heard him too. I even made some records once with him.
Yeah. He seemed powerful over the last few years of his life. He had a lot of power.

Well, now he oughta know when he was away at the time what I'm talking about. Man, he wasn't talking. That's a man just used to blow it. He didn't know a noda was as big as that lamp up there. He was a man. He used to blow it too. All you have to eat is run it, that's it. When he run a piece and it didn't take him too long to run it either. He played over once or twice and you come back there, he put in your gotcha.
Yeah. Did you ever play any advertising jobs with him at all?

Yeah, I used to play a couple of them at all. I had the mayor go around. Sometime he'd come up there and we'd run across a couple of bands around there, I'm telling you. We used to shake them up. Bunk, we had run across Bunk, not Bunk, or Punch. We had caught him. After you said something about records, I don't know if I just care to look. I'm more sure my wife got a book there of Bunk.
